Hi Marcus / Monica,

Quick note from our side — Q3 is shaping up faster than we expected and we need to increase our committed token capacity by ~45% starting July 1. Our current contract ends 2028-01-31 and procurement is asking for a clean path to add capacity without creating multiple standalone invoices across quarters.

Questions:
- Can you outline the options for a mid-contract top-up vs. annualizing and moving to a co-term (what proration looks like)?
- Any standard uplift discount you offer for mid-contract committed increases?
- Lead time for updated SOW / DocuSign if we choose to proceed next week?

Would prefer an option that keeps billing tidy and avoids a bunch of one-off invoices. Procurement is copied — they want the commercial terms to review.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Mid-year capacity increase — proration & co-term options

Amanda — thanks for the heads up and the forecast. High level we typically support two straightforward paths:

Option A — Top-up add-on (fastest)
- Add new committed capacity as a separate line item, prorated from the effective date to the existing contract term end.
- Billing: one pro-rata invoice for the remainder of the current term, then renewal invoices continue per the existing schedule.
- Discount: standard uplift discount of 5% on incremental committed units for mid-contract top-ups.
- Timing: fastest to implement (48–72 hours) once SOW signed.

Option B — Annualize + co-term (billing simplicity)
- Annualize the incremental capacity to create a single co-term that extends from the amendment effective date for 12 months; we then align the payment schedule to your preferred annual cadence.
- Billing: single consolidated invoice and a simplified renewal next year.
- Discount: for annualizing mid-cycle we can offer a deeper uplift discount — 12% on net-new committed capacity (requires a 12-month commitment on the annualized portion).
- Credit: as a one-time concession we can apply a 2-month billing credit toward the existing term to offset double-billing concerns.
- Timing: needs legal + procurement sign-off; target 5–7 business days for DocuSign + SOW update.

Option C — Hybrid (staged annualize)
- Immediate top-up as Option A for July, with auto-annualize at next quarter close if usage stabilizes. Discount: 8% on the portion annualized.

I attached a quick pricing-scenarios workbook with numbers based on the 45% uplift and three example cadence choices to show TCO impact and invoice timing (pricing-scenarios.xlsx).

Guidance items we need from you to finalize a clean recommendation:
- Exact effective date for the new capacity (you indicated July 1).
- Whether procurement prefers a single annualized invoice vs monthly/quarterly billing.
- Any internal constraints on co-term length (do you want the annualized portion to roll into your 2028 renewal or start a new 12-month clock?).

If you want, I can propose a single recommended path (my default would be Option B for accounting simplicity) and Monica can pull together the amendment and SOW.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Marcus — quick internal note before we lock anything in with Amanda / procurement. Thoughts:

- Lean toward Option B (annualize + co-term) to avoid messy mid-term invoices.
- Given margin pressure we should not go below 10% uplift discount on net-new committed capacity. 12% is OK if we can protect it with a 12-month firm commitment and include a 6-month ramp clause.
- Offer the 2-month credit as a one-time concession but make it contingent on signed amendment within 7 business days.

Grace/Ben — can you confirm whether legal needs any special SOW language for the ramp clause and whether billing can produce the consolidated invoice by EOD Friday if procurement signs?

Thx — Monica
